Topic 4.2: Spelling instruction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Spelling instruction. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters 
2. use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166
3. use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SPELLING INSTRUCTION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Spelling instruction helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SPELLING INSTRUCTION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters 

What this means
In this part you learn to spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Spelling instruction”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters . Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166

What this means
In this part you learn to use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Spelling instruction to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs

What this means
In this part you learn to use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Spelling instruction is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Spelling instruction”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters )

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Spelling instruction to a partner. (skill: use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Spelling instruction to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters .
3. Practise this skill: use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166.
4. Practise this skill: use simple editing strategies to  Learners practice spelling sight words correct spelling in simple  Learners participate in spelling sentences challenge contest, individually, in pairs.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Spelling instruction from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Spelling instruction: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Spelling instruction?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Spelling instruction means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: spell words with short and long of letter, sound correspondences, and vowel sounds and consonant common letter patterns clusters .
5. Be able to: use phonic knowledge to spell writing or unknown texts and provide and write familiar and correct spelling(spacing, punctuation, unfamiliar words and spelling) 166.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
